name: Senar de Kankalaba
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Traoré, Daouda. 2015. Table des matières (DNB scan of the same book).
sources.note: TOC only: phonology chapter sections are consonants, vowels, syllable structures, tonal system; no accent/stress heading.

sources.citation: Traoré, Daouda. 2015. Le senar (langue senufo du Burkina Faso): éléments de description et d'influence du jula véhiculaire dans un contexte de contact de langues. Göttingen: Cuvillier. xvii+422 pp. ISBN 978-3-95404-954-7 (Open Access e-book 978-3-7369-4954-6).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Ch. 1 Phonologie (pp. 24-69) has 1.4 'Le système tonal' (pp. 65-68): two contrastive tone registers H and L (agreeing with Bassinga-Traoré 1989: 60), a conditioned mid tone treated as downstep, contour tones HL and LH; the phonology summary (1.5, pp. 68-69) mentions only tone as suprasegmental. The word 'accent' occurs once in the whole book and only as 'forme accentuée' of the phrase-final marker kè (syntax chapter); no 'intensité', 'proéminence', 'stress' or 'prosodie' passages.

sources.note: Verbal morphology article (Niankorodougou data from D. Ouattara's 2023 MA thesis); only prosodic remark is p. 17 'Les tons sons systématiquement notés : ton haut ( ́) et ton bas ( ̀)'. Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Internal reconstruction of proto-Senufo phonetics from comparative lexical series; 'Seront examinés successivement les consonnes, les voyelles et, beaucoup plus sommairement, les tons.' Cited by Traoré 2015: 65 n. 42 (p. 288) for the phonological relevance of three punctual tones (H, M, L) in many Senufo languages, against which Traoré sets Senar's two-height system. What it says about Senar tone specifically is unseen.
